name: WNPS Conservation Grants
summary: Small reimbursement grants for native plant materials in on-the-ground ecosystem restoration projects in Washington State; applicants must be WNPS members, acting alone or for chapters and other organisations.
reporting: A final report of at least 300-500 words with documentation and photos suitable for publication.

eligibility.rule: Applicant or contact person is a WNPS member throughout the grant period
Project aligns with the WNPS Mission and Conservation Principles
Project furthers Washington native plant conservation and provides public benefit
Has received fewer than 3 WNPS awards in the past 6 years
Project budget excludes a stipend and work hours

status.quote: The Application due date is now passed, and the cycle is closed.

applicant_types.quote: Grant requests from WNPS members on behalf of WNPS chapters, other organizations, or individuals will be considered.

geography.quote: Proposals must further the conservation of Washington native plants and provide public benefit.

access.quote: Send electronic application copies (less than 5 MB total) to both

window.quote: WNPS provides small grants annually to further the mission around the state in 3 categories.

amount.quote: The WNPS Conservation Committee is soliciting proposals for Conservation Grants of up to $2000 each.

reporting.quote: The final report will be at least 300-500 words in length and will include documentation and photos suitable for publication by WNPS.

effort.quote: Send electronic application copies (less than 5 MB total) to both: conservationgrants@wnps.org and wnps@wnps.org with a subject line: WNPS Conservation Grant 2026.

eligibility.quote: The applicant or contact person must be a WNPS member throughout the grant period

Projects must align with the WNPS Mission, "To promote the appreciation and conservation of Washington's native plants and their habitats through study, education and advocacy," And the Principles of the WNPS Conservation Principles, available here.
Proposals must further the conservation of Washington native plants and provide public benefit.
Recipients will be limited to 3 awards in a 6-year period.
Funding is not available for a stipend or work hours.
